Paint ONE new 16:9 background screen for a point-and-click adventure game.

Place: the old core of Čierna Voda on Pezinská street (municipality Chorvátsky Grob, near Bratislava, Slovakia). Images 1-3 are dashcam photos of this real street: low single-storey village houses of the 1950s-70s with pitched red-brown tiled roofs and two-coloured plaster (image 1: pale peach and light blue), a house overgrown with a climbing vine (image 2), old stone walls, wooden gates with small tiled canopies, brick-paved pavements with a gravel and grass verge, and concrete electricity poles with wires (image 3). Paint grandmother Mira's property from these real house types, walls and materials - an invented house, not a copy of one particular house.

Brief: the gate of grandmother Mira's older little garden, seen from the street. A small outdoor table for leaving the shopping in front of the gate, a doorbell, and a window of her house in the background. There is no entry into the house: Mira is in quarantine. Time: a sunny autumn afternoon in October 2020, warm low sunlight, yellowing vine leaves, a few fallen leaves on the pavement. Small 2020 details: a small bottle of hand sanitiser at the edge of the table and a paper note with illegible scribbles taped to the gate.

Behind it a narrow strip of grass and gravel verge with fallen leaves, then Mira's garden boundary runs parallel to the picture plane; its foot meets the ground at about y 400. The boundary is a low old wall of stone and plaster with a weathered green wooden fence on top, about chest high. Behind it the older garden and, in the background, Mira's single-storey house with a pitched red-brown tiled roof and two-coloured plaster; one of its closed windows with lace curtains is clearly visible above the fence on the right (around x 1300-1600, y 40-300). Directly behind the table is the garden gate itself: a narrow old metal-and-wood pedestrian gate painted green, between two plastered gate pillars, under a small tiled gate canopy; an old two-tone doorbell button on the right pillar, no name on it.
